newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels kill four soldiers, blockade road.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels kill four soldiers, blockade road.

text.p: Four soldiers were killed and at least eight people were wounded when leftist rebels ambushed an army convoy in northwest Colombia, military officials said on Friday.

The attack took place near the town of Taraza in Antioquia province on Thursday afternoon. Two of those wounded were civilians, and two soldiers captured in the attack were still missing, an army spokesman said. He said Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas were responsible for the ambush.
In the Llorona Canyon region of the same province, FARC rebels set up a partial blockade of a key highway that links the trouble-torn banana-growing region of Uraba to central Colombia.
The army spokesman said the blockade was sporadic but had severely disrupted truck and bus traffic because drivers were frightened of coming under attack.
The FARC blockaded the same stretch of highway for one week in mid-September. The army called in air strikes and killed at least 25 rebels before they were able to clear the road.
